title: Signal drift notes — candidate Bryce Chen
short_summary: Rough pass after loop with B. Chen. Strong systems intuition; weaker offline benchmarking rigor. Risk: edge-case GC/kv-cache behavior, some performance assumptions unvalidated.
recommendation: hold - schedule follow-up focused on latency regression debugging and a whiteboard GC/kv-cache thought experiment. If follow-up goes well, lean hire (6->7).
content:
Context / purpose:
- Quick scratchpad after candidate loop (pair + design + on-call scenario). NOT polished. Keeping raw quotes and gut so we don't lose signal.

Panel: 
- Pairing: Lena M. (runtime), Kenji I. (infra) 
- Design / architecture: Omar (serving-runtime) 
- Behavioral/onsite portion: me (Priya)

Raw impressions (fast):
- Very comfortable with GPU/IPC tradeoffs and quantization tradeoffs. Talks like someone who’s built an inference stack.
- Repeatedly defaulted to optimistic perf numbers without citing measurement plan. When pressed, sketched a reasonable benchmarking matrix but didn’t tie to specific latencies/cost math.
- Good intuition for KV cache invalidation but missed a subtle race I asked about — our prefix re-use scenario under autoscale.
- On-call answers were pragmatic but lacked escalation discipline examples (who to loop in, SLO vs SLA trade-offs).

Key excerpts I scribbled: (verbatim-ish)
- “We can probably avoid a full KV eviction by sharding cache per-request signature.” (good start, need to probe memory overhead)
- “If we repro with a 256->4096 sequence boundary the throughput will halve, but we can window the kernel.” (said confidently but didn’t provide data plan)

Strengths:
- Systems-first mental model; low-level kernel/throughput intuition.
- Fast at sketching a rollout plan (canary -> ramp -> metric gating).
- Comfortable with Rust/C++ (says shipped runtime code), we should verify in take-home.

Risks / Open questions:
- Measurement rigor: doesn't have a ready-made perf harness story. Mentions "we used iperf-style microbenchmarks" — vague.
- KV cache GC race in autoscale/eviction scenario: candidate missed the scenario where two actors evict the same prefix mid-request (probable bug pattern for us).
- On-call escalation and communication: example answers were process-y, but lacked concrete postmortem examples.
- Cultural: not explicitly collaborative in pair, tended to push a preferred approach quickly (ok but watch for dogfooding).

Follow-up tasks / interview to schedule:
1) 45-60m focused follow-up: give a small reproducer (toy runtime) with a synthetic KV cache + autoscaler stub. Ask candidate to: a) find a latency regression, b) design a fix, c) outline test harness to prove it. Assess: debugging process, hypothesis formation, test design.
2) Take-home (optional): small PR to repo with unit tests + a perf script (we'll judge code quality + measurement clarity).
3) Behavioral: ask for a concrete postmortem where their change caused user-facing regression and what they did (timeline, stakeholders, follow-up).

Specific follow-up prompt sketch (for engineering interviewer):
- Repo: minimal runtime/kv-sim (toy). Two threads: request handler (reads prefix, may extend KV), and evictor (runs TTL/eviction every x ms) under load. Under scenario A (burst), requests experience 150-400ms tail latencies. Candidate must: 1) show how they'd instrument to find culprit, 2) propose fix (optimistic locking? per-shard GC?), 3) discuss tradeoffs (memory vs latency vs throughput).

Suggested scoring rubric for follow-up:
- Debugging process: 1-5 (did candidate form and test clear hypotheses?)
- Fix design: 1-5 (correctness + simplicity + testability)
- Measurement plan: 1-5 (does candidate propose repeatable benchmarks and metrics?)
- Code hygiene: 1-5 (if take-home completed)

Ramp/role fit notes:
- Likely to contribute early to kernel selection heuristics, batching strategy, and rollout gating.
- Might need mentoring on measurement culture and explicit SLO design. Plan: pair with SRE/observability for first 30 days to build bench skills.

Compensation note (private):
- Candidate asked about comp band during loop: mid-senior expectations (range shared verbally). Need recruiter confirm.

Panel action items (for me):
- Run scheduled follow-up with Kenji as technical lead. Kenji to prepare reproducer (assign JIRA).
- Lena to draft take-home starter repo (small).
- I will ask recruiting to confirm comp band and candidate availability.

Ticket seeds:
- JIRA-REQ-3172 (follow-up reproducer) — link above in linked_artifacts.
- If follow-up looks good create hiring recommendation doc.

Final gut:
- Candidate is promising in core runtime thinking, but our main gating signal is measurement/test-first mentality. If we can observe clear debugging + repeatable benchmarks in follow-up, this becomes a hire.
- Current lean: HOLD for focused follow-up (nonblocking).

Notes to self (odd fragments to not forget):
- Ask about memory alignment and sub-page allocations — they mentioned arena allocs but not fragmentation metrics.
- Probe for how they set cache TTLs in systems with millions of active prefixes.
- Confirm Github contributions (look for recent PRs in runtime repo).

End of scratchpad.
